1	# Project Landing Page - notes
2	
3	A project's own page (`/f/<id>`), a redesign of `server/views/_folder.eta` (with
4	`_branch.eta`), whose model is built in `server/main.js` (`view()` in the
5	`/f/:id` handler). Home (prelude/landing-page) gathers what needs the person
6	across projects and links here; this page holds the project's whole picture.
7	
8	Pages: `/f/:project` (Project), `/f/:project/designs/new` (New design, modal),
9	`/f/:project/branches/:branch/publish` (Push a branch, modal). Fragments:
10	`/f/:project/work`, `/f/:project/app`. States: typical (spark-lending), new
11	project, app being built, update clashed (with the app on the shell's branch
12	and a failed push), long names (an existing app to connect, no remote),
13	large project (a hundred features).
14	
15	## Decisions (the person asked for all eleven, 2026-10-18)
16	
17	1. **On the design system**, not ds/v1 + `prelude.css`, like Home.
18	2. **Work beside setup**: a `.split` in a `.center.wide`. Main: Needs you, In
19	   progress, Designs. Side: The app, What the agent can read. Added
20	   `.center.wide` / `--measure-wide` to the design system (46rem can't hold a
21	   split).
22	3. **New design is a modal**, opened by the header's "New design…", the page's
23	   one primary action. A refused title comes back into the fields alone
24	   (`_new-design-fields`); made, the modal closes and the page refreshes (the
25	   real app opens the new design's page).
26	4. **One primary per view**: Merge, Push, Start the app build are plain buttons.
27	5. **A branch's state as pills**: check, building / build stopped, behind main,
28	   pull request open, nothing done yet. Stories get a state pill (Built, To
29	   build, Building) and "A change". "Also changes" is a disclosure with the
30	   full list.
31	6. **Designs show progress**: pages and how many approved or built, and when
32	   they last changed. Grouped by area, those with none (system, shell) first.
33	   A plain "Ready to build" pill when

4	  *shown-on: /f/:project @ typical*
5	- **R-2hx.** A design with a branch is listed under In progress and not under Designs; once its branch is finished, it's listed under Designs again.
6	  *shown-on: /f/:project @ typical*
7	- **R-k4n.** Pushing a branch is always asked first, saying which branch goes to which remote, and nothing is pushed until the person says yes.
8	  *shown-on: /f/:project/branches/:branch/publish @ typical*

10	- **R-wm3.** New design offers the design system and the app shell as kinds only until the project has one of each.
11	  *shown-on: /f/:project/designs/new @ new-project*
12	- **R-r6b.** A design under Designs says it's ready to build when it has approved pages not yet built, and only once the project's app exists.

14	- **R-h2w.** Once the app is built, it can be run from the project's own folder with a command and address of its own, never the design host's, and the Run button always shows the command it runs, so clicking it is the approval.

19	  *proposed*

1	# The design system and app shell say what they hold
2	
3	For anyone looking down a project's designs to see how far each has got. Today the design system and the app shell are counted by their pages, as a feature is. The design system has no pages: its screens are a gallery of components. The shell's gallery is left out on purpose. So both say "nothing designed yet", or count gallery screens as pages, even when they're finished and in use. Once this is built, each one describes itself by what it actually holds. A person can then tell at a glance that they're done and don't need any more work.
4	
5	## What changes
6	
7	- Under Designs, the design system's line counts its components, e.g. "tokens and 24 components", rather than pages.
8	- The app shell's line counts its layouts, and any pages of its own beside them, e.g. "2 layouts" or "3 layouts and 1 page".
9	- Once the project's app exists, the shell's line also says how much of that is built: "all built", "1 built" or "none built yet". Before the app exists, it gives only the count.
10	- A design system with no components yet, or a shell with no layouts or pages, still says "nothing designed yet".
11	- Feature designs are counted by their pages, as they are today.
12	
13	## Acceptance criteria
14	
15	- In a project whose design system has components, its row under Designs reads "tokens and N components" (with "1 component" when there is only one), followed by when it last changed.
16	- A design system with no components reads "nothing designed yet".
17	- The app shell's row reads "N layouts". When the shell has pages of its own, the row reads "N layouts and M pages", with "layout" and "page" in the singular for one.
18	- When the project's app exists, the shell's row ends with "all built" when every layout and page is built. When only some are built, it ends with how many are built. When none is built, it ends with "none built yet".
19	- When the project's app doesn't exist yet, the shell's row gives the count

**Views** (`server/views/projects/`)
- **`_app`**: ported from the design. Once the app is built, the card has four forms. When nothing is set yet it asks for a command and address with "Save and run". While starting it shows a pulse and Stop. While running it shows Running, the address, Open and Stop. When stopped or failed it shows Run, with the command it runs right beside the button, and a "Change how it runs" section you can open.
- **`_run-fields`**: new, the command and address fields.
- **`_branch`**: gains the line saying what an update brought in. I left out the design's hidden `updated.from` and `updated.files` inputs, because they stood in for numbers the app now works out itself.
- **`page`**: the app card now also reloads on `app-changed`.
- **`_work`**: already matched the design, so it's unchanged.
- No styles changed.

**Model** (`server/project.js`): `app.run` (command, address, state, log) and an optional `inProgress[].updated` (`from`, `files`), typed from the states.

**Handlers** (`server/main.js`)
- `POST …/app/run` saves the settings, and starts the app too when it came from "Save and run". A refusal comes back as a 422 with the fields and what was wrong.
- `…/app/run/start` and `…/app/run/stop` both answer with the app card.
- After an update from main, the work's answer says how many files came in, or that there was nothing new.

**Rules**
- **R-h2w / R-5tj**: the new runner, `server/runs.js`, starts the app from the project's own folder. It gets its own `PORT` and never `PRELUDE_HOST`. It opens in the browser once something answers at its address. It's stopped, with everything it started, when Prelude quits.
- **Address checks**: the address must be on this computer, and can't be the design host's or Prelude's own.
- **R-p7c**: the instructions for building and for connecting an app now ask the agent to write `"run": { "start", "url" }` into `prelude/prelude.json`. A change made on the card is kept only on this computer, in `runs.json` in Prelude's home, and takes priority.
- **R-u9d**: "Update from main" now merges the remote's main only when it contains everything in the local main. Otherwise it merges the local one, so every commit the branch is counted behind comes in.

All four rules are no longer marked proposed in RULES.md, and every route in routes.json now points at the app's views. NOTES.md has a "Built" section listing where the app differs from the design.

**Before approving the screens and opening the pull request:**
- **Screens to compare**:

  - The large-project app card: nothing set, so it asks for both.
  - Document upload in large project: "main had nothing new for this branch".
- **The design-host clash is still unsolved**: on a .NET project, running the app while the design host runs in the same folder may fight over `bin/obj`. It's still listed under Open questions in NOTES.md.
- **Refusing a change without script**: the error comes back but what was typed is lost; the fields show what's saved. With script, it comes back as typed.
